title: Object-level authorization / IDOR / BOLA
content:
IDOR vulnerabilities are most commonly associated with horizontal privilege escalation, but they can also arise in relation to vertical privilege escalation.

Attackers can exploit API endpoints that are vulnerable to broken object-level authorization by manipulating the ID of an object that is sent within the request.

Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) occurs when an API does not properly enforce authorization checks for each object accessed by the client.

Object level authorization is an access control mechanism that is usually

on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks.

Insecure direct object references (IDOR) are a type of access control vulnerability that arises when an application uses user-supplied input to access objects directly.

The objective of this test is to identify whether the API enforces proper object-level authorization checks, ensuring that users can only access and manipulate objects they are authorized to interact with.

Object Ownership Checks : Ensure that object-level authorization checks are performed for every API request.
